title: path
lede: Node's `path` module for portable filesystem path manipulation, import-gated as a virtual built-in (`import path from 'path'`). Both of Node's flavours exist on every host: a bare `path` is the host's flavour (`path.win32` on Windows — backslashes, `;`, drive letters, UNC roots — and `path.posix` on Linux/macOS), while `path.posix.*` and `path.win32.*` name one explicitly. join, resolve, dirname, basename, extname, parse/format and isAbsolute follow real Node's algorithms in both flavours, including its asymmetric `basename` extension-stripping rule; the win32 flavour is a C port of Node's own `lib/path.js`.

entries.name: path.join(...segments)
entries.description: Joins segments with the flavour's separator, then normalizes the result: collapses repeated separators, drops `.` segments, and resolves `..` against segments already seen in the same call. The win32 flavour accepts mixed `/` and `\`, keeps UNC and drive roots intact, and never lets `..` escape a drive root.

entries.name: path.resolve(...segments)
entries.description: Absolute-always: starts from `process.cwd()` and keeps only the last absolute segment and what follows it, as in real Node. The win32 flavour also tracks the drive: a segment rooted on another drive wins, a drive-relative segment (`C:x`) resolves against that drive's own current directory, and a rooted-but-driveless segment (`\abs`) takes `cwd`'s drive.

entries.name: path.dirname(p)
entries.description: Directory portion of a path; trailing slashes are trimmed first.

entries.name: path.basename(p, ext?)
entries.description: Final path segment, optionally with a trailing `ext` stripped — not stripped when doing so would consume the whole segment, unless the entire `path` argument equals `ext` (then returns `""`), matching real Node's own asymmetric rule here.

entries.name: path.extname(p)
entries.description: Extension of the basename, including the leading `.`; returns `""` for a dotfile whose only `.` is its first character.

entries.name: path.parse(p) / path.format(obj)
entries.signature: parse(p: string): { root, dir, base, ext, name }; format(obj): string
entries.description: `parse` returns `{root, dir, base, ext, name}`; `format` is the inverse (`base` wins over `name`+`ext`, `dir` falls back to `root`).

returns.desc: A parsed path object, or a reassembled string.

entries.name: path.isAbsolute(p)
entries.description: True when the path is absolute: `p[0] === '/'` for posix; for win32 a leading `/` or `\` (including UNC) or a drive letter followed by a separator, so drive-relative `C:x` is not absolute.

entries.name: path.sep / path.delimiter
entries.description: The path-segment separator and the PATH-style delimiter, as compile-time constants for the host's flavour: `/` and `:` on Linux/macOS, `\` and `;` on Windows.
entries.snippet:
console.log(path.sep)       // / (\ on Windows)
console.log(path.delimiter) // : (; on Windows)
console.log(path.win32.sep) // \ on every host

entries.name: path.posix / path.win32
entries.description: The two flavour objects Node exposes on every platform. Each carries the same method set as `path` — join, resolve, dirname, basename, extname, isAbsolute, parse, format, sep, delimiter — with posix or Windows semantics regardless of the host. A bare `path` dispatches to the host's flavour.
differences: The flavour objects are dispatch targets, not first-class values — call `path.win32.join(...)` or import the object by name (`import { win32 } from 'path'`); binding it to a variable first is not supported.
`normalize`, `relative`, `toNamespacedPath` and `matchesGlob` are missing from both flavours.

entries.name: path.normalize(p) / path.relative(from, to) / path.toNamespacedPath(p)
entries.signature: normalize(p: string): string; relative(from: string, to: string): string; toNamespacedPath(p: string): string
entries.description: `normalize` resolves `.`/`..` and repeated separators and keeps a trailing separator. `relative` resolves both ends against `process.cwd()` and walks up with `..`; the win32 flavour compares case-insensitively and returns `to` outright across drives or UNC shares. `toNamespacedPath` is the identity for posix and the resolved `\\?\C:\…` / `\\?\UNC\…` long-path form for win32. All three exist in both flavours.

returns.desc: The normalized, relative, or namespaced path.
